title: Studio condition builder writes list membership in the spelling the validator now rewrites (after #36340)
body:
repo:objectstack#7 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jTeURPvEm465RcoYEC

Follow-up from #36167 (PR #36340). Found by the L2 record 7076594662 on PR #36340; filed by the seat. Parent: #36167.

## What happens

The merged Studio condition builder (#36185) writes list membership as `S != null && V in S`. PR #36340's own measurement says that spelling faults on a sparse action row and on a null `previous`. After #36340 the validator (`checkListEquality`, `listMembershipRewrite`) prescribes a different, per-site spelling for a `record.` read. So the builder and the validator now prescribe different spellings for the same site: an author who builds a condition in Studio can get a form the validator would rewrite, or one that faults at run time.

## To do

1. Make the builder emit exactly what `listMembershipRewrite` prescribes for each site (record-triggered start condition, action row, `previous`), by calling the same helper rather than restating it.
2. Fix the `checkListEquality` docblock's opening line, which still names `S != null && V in S` as "the prescription" (N1 of the same record).

## Acceptance

- A test builds a membership condition in the builder at each of the three sites and asserts that the validator accepts it unchanged and that the engine evaluates it without a fault on a sparse row and on a null `previous`.

Blocked-by: #36340 (the per-site prescription must be on `main` first)

## Grade
p2 · area:build · domain:ui. Two halves of one feature disagree, and a builder-written condition can fault at run time.
